payload.summary: CLEAN-SIGNALS-STRANDED-STATE-SWEEP-FILES-PERMANENT-DRAIN-LITTER (P3, backlog) is understated: its status_note enumerates 3 residue files, but the same never-drains class now has at least 7 members. Fold, do not mint a duplicate.
payload.diagnosis: The three price_anomaly_* files are VALID JSON but carry no signal envelope: keys are {schema, generated_at, dish_window, tickers}, schema=price_anomaly_v1, dish_window=eod, ~34 tickers each. They are data artifacts written into the signal DROP directory, not signals. Because they parse, drain-signals.js emits no diagnostic at all for them -- unlike the parse-invalid file, which at least logs 'SKIP unparseable'. Silent-skip is the more dangerous of the two failure modes: zero operator signal, indefinite accumulation.
payload.producer_lead: price_anomaly_v1 with dish_window=eod points at a chef/market EOD producer, not at an agent signal emitter. Dated 2026-08-12, 08-13, 08-14 on consecutive days then stopping suggests a short-lived misconfiguration rather than a still-active writer -- confirm before fixing, the emitter may already be retired (row AC-3 allows 'confirmed retired' as a valid outcome).
payload.why_it_matters: Row AC-4 already asks for an explicit disposition for shape-invalid files so they are quarantined on first sight instead of re-skipped forever. That AC is the structural fix for this whole class; the price_anomaly trio is evidence the class keeps growing while the row sits in backlog at P3. The residue is also a fixed floor under the >50 DRAIN-BEHIND alert the row itself cites -- at 50 top-level files that floor is now materially close to the alert threshold.
